title: Verifier-Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We study whether integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM-alone proposals. Using a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1) we synthesized a Cornetto-like multi-vendor set of 200 confirmatory intent→configuration tasks stratified by topology scale, and executed paired episodes with gpt-5-mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM-alone generation) and guarded (LLM + deterministic verifier + single repair iteration). Primary outcome = paired difference in per-task functional-regression rate. On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes), guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840, respectively; paired difference = 0.015957 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.037234], exact McNemar two-sided p=0.25). The preregistered effect size (≥0.20 absolute reduction) was not observed. We release preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, and analysis artifacts. We discuss ceiling effects, verifier scope, missingness, and implications for verifier-guided NetOps workflows.

sections.introduction: Modern NetOps prototypes increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to translate operator intent into low‑level device configuration. While LLMs can generate executable configuration artifacts, operator adoption depends on operational reliability: the generator must avoid introducing functional regressions or unsafe intermediate states. Prior work has proposed generate→validate→repair architectures and verifier-augmented agents to improve safety (e.g., CRITIC-style tool interaction, formal verifiers and translation approaches). However, evidence quantifying the incremental benefit of a deterministic verifier in a paired, preregistered comparison is limited. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce the rate of functional regressions and the average blast radius of repairs versus an LLM-alone pipeline on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experimental design (CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1) grounded in a reproducible Cornetto-like synthetic task generator; (2) a deterministic execution and analysis pipeline (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) applying gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (3) the confirmatory result reported from archived execution artifacts and the full evidence bundle.
sections.related_work: We position this study relative to two strands. First, benchmarks and pipelines for LLM-driven configuration and repair (e.g., Cornetto-style benchmarking for functional repair at scale) provide task-generation and oracle evaluation methods used here. Second, verifier- or constraint-based guardrails and tool-interactive self-correction (e.g., CRITIC; verifier-augmented agent proposals) motivate the guarded condition. Complementary work argues for translation-to-formal-model approaches (TypoNet, SymNet) and constraint-guided LLM adaptation (MeshAgent). Unlike prior open benchmark studies that compare many models, our contribution is a preregistered, paired, within-task evaluation isolating verifier impact under a single-model, operationally interpretable estimator.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered the study (ID CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1; preregistration SHA-256: feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) before observing outcomes. Confirmatory plan: paired design with 200 stratified tasks (small/medium/large topology scale) and a target primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary hypothesis H1: absolute reduction ≥0.20 in regression rate (guarded vs baseline). Task generation and oracle: tasks were synthesized with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 into intent→golden configuration pairs; golden configs and seeded faults were the ground truth. Models and pipeline: all generation used gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) with a shared initial candidate semantics; guarded condition invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to validate the candidate and allow a single automated repair iteration when the verifier reported violations. Execution and logging: adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed episodes in Dockerized containers; all prompts, raw model outputs, verifier traces, and hashes were archived. Analysis plan: primary inference used exact McNemar paired-proportion test and 95% bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 reps; seed archived). Missingness: policy 'complete_pair_primary' excluded pairs where both episodes failed; sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as regressions were preregistered. Stopping and deviations: execution manifest recorded completion metadata and no post-hoc design changes were made.
sections.results: Execution summary: planned 400 episodes (200 pairs); completed 376 episodes; failed episodes 24; resulting complete pairs included in primary analysis = 188. Primary confirmatory outcome (archived analysis): baseline_success_count=185/188 (0.9840425531914894), guarded_success_count=188/188 (1.0). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap (10,000 reps, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149]. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute reduction ≥0.20) was not observed. Missingness and failures: 12 pairs were missing because both condition episodes failed (recorded in execution manifest); provider transient failures accounted for the majority of failed episodes and were handled per preregistered missingness rules. Repair activity: the guarded repair stage was invoked in a small number of tasks (stage_counts: repair=3) according to the execution manifest; archived verifier traces show no guarded-condition introductions of new functional regressions in the included pairs. Secondary estimands (blast-radius median difference) were specified as exploratory but are not reported as confirmatory findings in the archived results.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the point estimate favors the guarded pipeline but is small (≈1.6 percentage points) and statistically inconclusive under the preregistered test. Two operational factors limit effect size here: (1) high baseline correctness (≈98.4%) produces a ceiling effect that limits room for large absolute reductions; (2) the synthetic task set and the verifier scope (deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with explicit supported feature set) may have limited the instances where the verifier could detect and prevent dangerous LLM proposals. The small number of repair invocations (3 repair-stage calls logged) indicates that, for this task family and model, most LLM proposals satisfied the oracle or matched the golden answer, reducing observable verifier intervention. Threats to validity: internal — prompt sensitivity and single-model design (gpt-5-mini) restrict internal generality; construct — synthetic tasks approximate operational intent-to-config translation but omit production telemetry and emergent vendor idiosyncrasies; external — single-model, single-verifier, synthetic benchmark limit generalization to other models, verifiers, and production networks; conclusion validity — completed-pair count (188) limited power versus original 200 target due to failed episodes and the observed unexpectedly low discordant proportion, producing a non-significant p-value. Practical implication: verifier-guided pipelines remain an important safety architecture, but their measurable benefit depends on (a) baseline error-rate regime, (b) verifier coverage relative to the model's failure modes, and (c) task difficulty. For high baseline-success tasks the verifier may mostly act as an audit rather than a corrective mechanism. Future work should evaluate lower-baseline settings, richer failure injections, multi-model ensembles, and expanded verifier feature coverage.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, paired evaluation of a deterministic-verifier-augmented generate→validate→repair pipeline using gpt-5-mini on a Cornetto-like synthetic multi-vendor task set. The guarded pipeline produced a small positive point estimate (≈1.6 pp) in reducing functional regressions but did not meet the preregistered efficacy threshold (≥20 pp) and was not statistically significant (p=0.25). The evidence suggests that verifier impact is context dependent: when baseline LLM proposals are already highly correct on the task family used here, measurable verifier gains are small. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts to support follow-up studies and replication.

limitations: Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not imply generality across models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto-like benchmark — task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to real operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4%) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair-stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions on iterative repair dynamics and blast-radius effects.
